limitations_and_boundaries: PairNorm does not necessarily increase absolute performance on standard benchmarks because shallow networks (2-4 layers) suffice.
PairNorm-SI is used for GCN and GAT due to better stability, but the reason is not fully understood.
Hyperparameter s for PairNorm in SGC is tuned per dataset; for GCN/GAT s=1 fixed due to resource limitations.
Experiments limited to four datasets; generalizability to other graph types not tested.
PairNorm may cause slight performance drop at 0% missing rate because it reverses the beneficial smoothing effect of few layers.

research_questions.statement: How can oversmoothing in deep GNNs be mitigated to enable training of deeper models without performance degradation?

provenance.text_excerpt: Experiments on real-world graphs demonstrate that PAIRNORM makes deeper GCN, GAT, and SGC models more robust against oversmoothing, and significantly boosts performance for a new problem setting that benefits from deeper GNNs.

claims.statement: PairNorm makes deeper GCN, GAT, and SGC models more robust against oversmoothing and significantly boosts performance for settings that benefit from deeper GNNs.

provenance.text_excerpt: Our main contribution is PAIRNORM, a novel normalization layer that is based on a careful analysis of the graph convolution operator, which prevents all node embeddings from becoming too similar.

claims.statement: PairNorm prevents node embeddings from becoming too similar, tackling oversmoothing.

provenance.text_excerpt: What is more, PAIRNORM is fast, easy to implement without any change to network architecture nor any additional parameters, and is broadly applicable to any GNN.

claims.statement: PairNorm is fast, easy to implement, requires no architecture change or extra parameters, and is broadly applicable to any GNN.

experiments_or_tasks: Analyze graph convolution as Laplacian smoothing and define row-diff and col-diff measures to quantify oversmoothing.
Derive PairNorm as a center-and-scale procedure that keeps total pairwise squared distance constant.
Propose PairNorm normalization layer to prevent node embeddings from becoming too similar across layers.

methods.name: PairNorm
methods.protocol_description: A normalization layer applied after each graph convolution (except the last). It consists of centering (subtract row-wise mean) and scaling (divide by sqrt of mean squared norm of centered representations, then multiply by hyperparameter s). For SGC, PairNorm is used; for GCN and GAT, PairNorm-SI (scale individually) is used, which normalizes each node representation to have L2-norm s.

study_units.name: PairNorm method proposal and analysis

provenance.text_excerpt: Then, ˙X := PAIRNORM(˜X) has row-wise mean 0 (i.e., is centered) and constant total pairwise squared distance C = 2n2s2.

provenance.text_excerpt: Note that SGC has a fixed number of parameters that does not depend on the number of graph convolutions (i.e. layers). In effect, it is guarded against the influence of overfitting and vanishing gradient problem with more layers. This leaves us only with oversmoothing as a possible cause of performance degradation with increasing K.

claims.statement: Oversmoothing is a cause of performance degradation with increasing layers in SGC, as overfitting and vanishing gradients are controlled.

provenance.text_excerpt: While PAIRNORM enables deeper models that are more robust to oversmoothing, it may seem odd that the overall test accuracy does not improve. In fact, the benchmark graph datasets often used in the literature require no more than 4 layers, after which performance decays (even if slowly).

claims.statement: PairNorm enables deeper models that are more robust to oversmoothing, but overall test accuracy does not improve on standard benchmarks because shallow networks suffice.

provenance.text_excerpt: As we have proved, PAIRNORM normalizes APSD to be constant across layers, however it does not normalize APD, which appears to decrease linearly with increasing number of layers. Surprisingly, although PAIRNORM-SI is not theoretically proved to have a constant APSD and APD, empirically it achieves more stable APSD and APD than PAIRNORM.

results.value_raw_text: PairNorm normalizes APSD to be constant across layers; PairNorm-SI achieves more stable APSD and APD than PairNorm.
